Items.Authors: Nathan K. Long, Barnaby Norris, Daniel S. Dahl, Christopher H. Betters, Julia J. Bryant, Nick Cvetojevic, Sergio Leon-Saval, Frantz Martinache, Marc-Antoine Martinod, Akira Rodziewicz-Ryan, Adam Taras, Jin Wei, Peter Tuthill
Items.Title: Overcoming the low signal-to-noise problem for hybrid mode-selective photonic lantern-based wavefront correction using machine learning
Items.Abstract: Hybrid mode-selective photonic lanterns transform an input complex point-spread function into several single-mode outputs, where a selected core feeds the fundamental mode to a photonic science instrument, while the remaining cores are used for wavefront sensing in a closed-loop adaptive optics system. A neural network maps the intensities of the wavefront sensing cores to an estimated wavefront correction, which is applied to an upstream deformable mirror. However, there exists a trade between maximizing the amount of light reserved for the photonic instrument and the reduced signal-to-noise ratios for the wavefront sensing cores. We explore this trade-off using the Seidr instrument, a part of the Asgard Suite for the Very Large Telescope Interferometer. We evaluate different neural network architectures, benchmarked against null depths for high contrast and high angular resolution imaging with the Seidr instrument.

Items.Authors: Edvardas Vinerskas, Benoit Neichel, Angelie Alagao, Mathieu Motte, Vincent Chambouleyron, Cédric Taïssir Heritier, Thierry Fusco, Jean-François Sauvage, Romain Fetick, Jonathan Dray, Morgan Gray, Pierre Jouve
Items.Title: PAPYRUS @ OHP: controlling the 2nd stage with model-based reinforcement learning
Items.Abstract: In this work, we demonstrate a successful on-sky implementation of a model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) algorithm for the control of the PAPYRUS second stage adaptive optics system, which employs the state-of-the-art vector Zernike Wavefront Sensor. We demonstrate that the MBRL algorithm compensates for the temporal error and system misregistration. In addition, the MBRL algorithm successfully learns the non-linear nature of the vZWFS signal and achieves an inference time in the millisecond range, showing an overall improvement over traditional control methods. Hence, this work marks the next step in the control of adaptive optics systems for the purpose of high-contrast direct imaging of exoplanets.

Items.Authors: Francisco Antonio Oyarzun, Benoit Neichel, Thierry Fusco, Cedric-Taissir Heritier, Mathieu Motte, Vincent Chambouleyron, Angelie Alagao
Items.Title: PAPYRUS second stage: non-linear phase reconstruction of the Vector-Zernike wavefront sensor using a convolutional neural network
Items.Abstract: A second stage adaptive optics (AO) system was installed on the PAPYRUS instrument at Observatoire de Haute-Provence. The wavefront sensor of this second stage corresponds to a vector-Zernike (VZ) wavefront sensor (WFS), a highly sensitive but non-linear WFS. Traditional linear reconstruction techniques for the VZ WFS require a high degree of correction from the first stage, and any deviation from that could cause the second stage to diverge. To solve this issue and make the system more robust, we propose to use a convolutional neural network (CNN) as a non-linear phase reconstructor. The CNN can extend the dynamic range of the sensor by using the information scattered through the whole pupil to estimate the phase at each point. To do this, we developed a numerical twin of the second stage, trained the network with the twin, and tested it on the bench yielding better results than the linear reconstructor.

Items.Authors: Jeremy P. Scott, Steve Ertel, Thomas Stuber, Denis Defrère, Romain Laugier
Items.Title: Performance analysis of the Asgard/NOTT nulling interferometer: optimizing observing modes for high-contrast detection
Items.Abstract: This work reports on the simulated performance of the Asgard/NOTT visitor instrument at the VLTI, which uses integrated optics and nulling interferometry to suppress starlight and enable high-contrast detections of exoplanets and hot exozodiacal dust. We compare three distinct observing modes, discussing the trade-offs between each mode in terms of sensitivity, spatial information retention, and complexity. We then introduce the SCIFYsim simulation framework, adapted specifically for NOTT, and present the resulting performance metrics and optimal operational strategies for both exoplanet and hot exozodiacal dust science.

Items.Authors: Shotaro Tada, Kohei Miyakawa, Hirokazu Kataza, Ryouhei Kano, Takehiko Wada, Masanobu Ozaki, Fumihiko Usui, Iona Kondo, Yui Kasagi, Hajime Kawahara, Takayuki Kotani
Items.Title: Performance Characterization of an InGaAs NIR Sensor for the JASMINE Mission
Items.Abstract: JASMINE is a Japanese infrared astrometry mission under study for development toward a 2032 launch, aiming at astrometry of the Galactic center and a planet transit survey around M-dwarfs. Its focal plane will employ four domestically developed ~2k × 2k InGaAs near-infrared detectors. Building on the heritage of the ground-based InGaAs sensor (Nakaya et al. 2016), we are performing upgrades for space use. We have performed heavy-ion irradiation and vibration tests on prototypes and obtained favorable environmental results. Low-temperature vacuum tests yield ~70% QE at 1.0–1.5 μm and also confirm the temperature dependence of the quantum efficiency. This presentation reports these results and the current status of detector performance evaluation.

Items.Authors: Kenta Sakabe, Kenta Nakamura, Yoshimi Rokugawa, Florian Quatresooz, Hideki Takami, Mareki Honma, Takayuki Usami, Junichi Nakazono, Yuma Abe, Yoshihiko Saito
Items.Title: Performance evaluation of adaptive optics by horizontal-link experiments for ETS-9 optical communications
Items.Abstract: In satellite-to-ground optical communication, atmospheric turbulence reduces communication efficiency, but Adaptive Optics (AO) can increase it. National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT), Japan aims to achieve 10 Gbps communication on the Engineering Test Satellite 9 (ETS-9), scheduled for launch in fiscal year 2026 or later. As a preliminary demonstration test, a horizontal link experiment was conducted using NICT's Koganei 1m telescope and 40cm telescope. Performance evaluation tests were performed on the AO mounted on the 1m telescope. The tests were conducted over 22 days (5/2025 to 11/2025), during both daytime and nighttime periods. The results showed that the Fried parameter ranged from 10 to 30 cm at λ1.5 um. The residual wavefront error was found to be improved to less than 1/5. The coupling efficiency to the SMF achieved the 5 dB improvement targeted by ETS-9. This presentation reports on the performance of the AO in free space on more analysis.

Items.Authors: Matias Marambio-Jimenez, Yosuke Minowa, Yoshito Ono, Shin Oya, Yusei Koyama, Masayuki Akiyama
Items.Title: Performance of attention-based deep-learning models in Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor measurements
Items.Abstract: Recently, there has been substantial development in deep learning applications for wavefront sensing focused on pyramid wavefront sensors. However, the performance of these techniques has not been studied at length in conventional AO systems using Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensors (SHWFS) with advanced architectures such as Vision Transformers (ViT). This research aims to develop an innovative AO control system by applying ViT models directly to raw SHWFS outputs, leveraging the capabilities of the AO3K and ULTIMATE-START systems at the Subaru Telescope to generate robust training datasets. The core hypothesis is that this approach will outperform previous methods and convolutional models by using attention-based mechanisms and exploiting otherwise lost information from centroiding, enabling more accurate atmospheric turbulence correction and improved angular resolution in astronomical imaging. Furthermore, this research will benchmark on-sky performance in the Subaru telescope.

Items.Authors: Anders M. Jorgensen, John Young, Eugene Seneta, David Buscher, Andres Olivares, Chris Salcido, James Luis, Emma Floyd
Items.Title: Performance of real-time fringe-tracking software used with FOURIER at MROI
Items.Abstract: We report on the performance of the software fringe-tracking and observing system used with FOURIER. We will present details of the work to optimize the fringe phasor estimation algorithm, and the fringe-tracking performance. We will show results of using the fringe-tracker with data from FOURIER as well as simulated data.

Items.Authors: Grzegorz Krzysztof Szymanski, Piotr Wawer, Adam Sikorski, Przemysław Nita, Mateusz Sobiecki, Daniel Półtorak, Aleksandra Mirońska, Konrad R. Skup, Mirosław Rataj
Items.Title: Performance verification systems for ESA ARIEL FGS instrument
Items.Abstract: Fine Guiding System (FGS) is a highly advanced optical instrument developed by international Consortium led by CBK PAN in frame of ESA ARIEL space mission. Its goal is to observe atmospheres of exoplanes by providing scientific data using three photometric channels (FGS1, FGS2 and VISPhot) and one low resolution spectrometer (NIRSpec). To characterize the optical parameters of FGS, an advanced OGSE system was developed and verified at CBK PAN. The main parts of the system include: OGSE ILU which is responsible for providing proper wavelength and power level of light that will illuminate FGS; OGSE OMA which is used for integration and alignment of FGS; OGSE OMC which is responsible for beam forming in TVAC. This paper provides details on design and verification of each major OGSE subsystem.

Items.Authors: Amir Ebadati Bazkiaei, Brent Miszalski, Jesse van de Sande, Nuria Lorente, Simon O'Toole, Kate Sheng
Items.Title: PERRY: A Human-in-the-Loop GUI for Precision Alignment of MUSE Data
Items.Abstract: The Multi Unit Spectroscopic Explorer (MUSE) on the Very Large Telescope produces vast and complex datasets. Misalignments between multiple observations can introduce artifacts that compromise data quality. To address this, we have developed PERRY, a Python-based Graphical User Interface (GUI) for the manual inspection and fine-tuning of MUSE image alignments. Integrated as a quality assurance step within the Pythonic AAO Reduction Environment (PARE), PERRY acts on the outputs of an automated alignment recipe. PERRY provides a suite of interactive tools, including the ability to "blink" between reference and aligned images, dynamic contour overlays, and real-time linear fitting plots. Users can interactively shift and rotate images with user-defined precision, save their adjustments, and continue with the PARE pipeline. We present the architecture of PERRY, demonstrate its key features, and discuss its role in ensuring data quality within a modern astronomical data reduction workflow.

Items.Authors: Simon M. Tulloch, Fernando Abárzuza, Jorge Jiménez, Cristóbal Padilla
Items.Title: Persistence Characterisation of the ARRAKIHS NIR detectors.
Items.Abstract: We have developed a test bench for the characterisation of the 1.7um H2RG detectors for the ARRAKIHS space astronomy mission. An internal cold shutter allows the user to choose between an external light source for high-background work and total darkness for dark-current and persistence investigations. With the shutter closed, light can still be provided by internal cold NIR LEDs. These are mounted alongside the detector within an integrating volume that produces pseudo-flat field illumination. Characterisation work focuses on the time-constant distribution of persistence-inducing traps and the relationship between dark current and operating temperature but will later be extended to include measurements of Quantum Efficiency and cutoff wavelength.

Items.Authors: Noah H. Schwartz, Douglas Harvey, D. Scott Acton, Charlotte Bond, Ben Buky, Ailidh Kinney
Items.Title: Phasing of small deployable optical telescope using intensity measurements: laboratory demonstration
Items.Abstract: Segmented and deployable telescopes require precise phasing for diffraction-limited performance, but traditional wavefront sensing can be impractical for compact systems. We demonstrate three focal-plane strategies using only intensity measurements: (1) image-based metric optimisation for coarse alignment, (2) a closed-loop machine learning approach for rapid fine phasing, and (3) a JWST-inspired phase retrieval method achieving sub-wavelength accuracy. These techniques provide a low-complexity, robust solution for phasing small deployable telescopes, with strong potential for space-based platforms where size, weight, and power are critical.

Items.Authors: Ugo Lo Cicero, Marco Barbera, Philippe Peille, Lionel Jacques, Edoardo Cucchetti, Michela Todaro, Edoardo Alaimo, Luisa Sciortino, Fabio D'Anca, Federico Fiorentino
Items.Title: Photon shot-noise analysis for the NewAthena X-IFU reformulation
Items.Abstract: The X-IFU instrument on the NewAthena mission relies on Transition Edge Sensor microcalorimeters operating at millikelvin temperatures. To preserve the detector's high-resolution X-Ray spectroscopy, it must be shielded from out-of-band radiation (far-IR to extreme UV) that generates performance-degrading Photon Shot-Noise (PSN). A stack of thermal-optical filters is used to this end. In this paper we introduce "ray3cer," a custom ray-tracing software developed to model complex cavity effects and low-transmissivity filters. We highlight the critical role of these simulations during the recent instrument reformulation from the original Athena concept to the NewAthena design. Specifically, we show how PSN analysis drove the selection of the filter configuration, key element for ensuring that X-IFU meets its scientific performance requirements.

Items.Authors: Adam K. Taras, Louis Desdoigts, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert
Items.Title: PIAA-ZFWS: a practical and robust wavefront sensor that approaches the fundamental sensitivity limit
Items.Abstract: High-contrast imaging needs extremely sensitive wavefront sensing to correct atmospheric effects. While the limits of the sensitivity of a wavefront sensor are well known, a practical, robust design that saturates these limits remains elusive. This work proposes the PIAA-ZWFS (Phase-Induced Amplitude Apodization-Zernike Wavefront Sensor). We developed a framework to optimize its design, maximizing Fisher information per frame in the presence of both phase and amplitude aberrations. We present optimized designs for various bandwidths, mode bases, and telescope sizes (including ELTs). The PIAA-ZWFS can be optimized for noise (read/photon) or stellar magnitude range. Closed loop simulations show improved performance, nearly saturating the information bound for aberrations with high frequencies and surpassing classic sensors at low frequencies, making it a viable system for future adaptive optics.

Items.Authors: Eemil Halonen, Jalo Nousiainen, Markus Kasper, Nuutti Hyvönen
Items.Title: PiPO4AO: a WFS pixel-based policy optimization for adaptive optics control
Items.Abstract: Direct imaging of Earth-like exoplanets around nearby stars requires extreme AO (XAO) that delivers high contrast at very small angles. Performance is limited by fast XAO residuals and quasi-static speckles, requiring ultra-sensitive yet highly nonlinear wavefront sensors. Greater sensitivity amplifies the response to critical aberrations, such as low-wind-effect petal modes, but severely challenges conventional linear reconstructors. Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a powerful XAO control tool, with model-based RL variants already reducing latency, misregistration, and moderate nonlinearities. We present a fully model-free RL model that directly maps raw nonlinear WFS intensities to DM commands, eliminating reconstruction matrices. The end-to-end approach significantly extends sensor dynamic range and linearity. Closed-loop performance is validated in high-fidelity simulations and on the GHOST cascaded-XAO testbench at ESO Garching.

Items.Authors: Giacomo Cherchi, Natalia Auricchio, Fabrizio Cogato, Isabella Pagano, Gianalfredo Nicolini, Elisabetta Tommasi
Items.Title: PLATO camera as-built configuration data list: configuration management and automation with Python tools
Items.Abstract: PLATO is ESA's M3 mission to detect and characterise exoplanets around bright solar-type stars using high-precision space photometry. The payload uses a multi-telescope concept with 26 Cameras (CAMs) produced in series by several institutions. For each CAM, the configuration is reported in an As-Built Configuration Data List (ABCL), which gathers serial numbers, procedures, reports, configuration/calibration files and tracks Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs) and Request for Deviation/Waiver (RFD/W) throughout Assembly, Integration, Testing and Verification (AIT/V) phases. In total, this corresponds to about 1000 items, 1200 documents and over 60 ABCL issues. After introducing the general framework, in this presentation, we present a Python-based workflow, built around a central Excel database and a controlled set of keywords, that automatically generates CAM ABCLs, ensuring consistent as-built data, efficient tracking of NCRs and RFD/W, and a global overview of the PLATO camera population

Items.Authors: Lars Hagge, Markus Garczarczyk, Anja Maaß, Terhi Maibaum, Alexander Steiner
Items.Title: PLM-based digital fabrication planning, control and progress tracking of the CTAO Medium-Sized Telescopes (MSTs)
Items.Abstract: The CTAO plans to build nine Medium-Sized Telescopes (MST) at its Northern site in La Palma (Canaries, Spain), and fourteen at its Southern site in Paranal (Chile). Two pathfinder telescopes are currently being fabricated for the Southern site. A key objective of the pathfinders is to prepare for subsequent series production. For this, the entire fabrication process is digitalized based on a PLM system, which serves as a central collaboration platform and supports the management of a widely distributed manufacturing workflow. The presentation outlines the fabrication process and its challenges, introduces the digitalized fabrication control solution, and summarizes the current status, experience gained, and lessons learned.

Items.Authors: Yuxuan Zhu, Yusa Wang, Vadim Burwitz, Yifan Zhang, Zijian Zhao, Xiongtao Yang, Yanji Yang, Surangkhana Rukdee, Gisela Hartner
Items.Title: Preliminary cross calibration results of the X-ray mirror engineering module onboard eXTP
Items.Abstract: This paper presents preliminary cross-calibration for mirror module 3 (MM3) of the eXTP focusing mirror, conducted at both the 100XF and PANTER facilities, focusing on point spread functions (PSFs), vignetting, and effective area.   The cross-calibration results validate the reliability of the calibration methodologies for eXTP mirrors.

Items.Authors: Dehbia Lattab, Diego Götz, Eric Doumayrou, Aline Meuris, Frédéric Pinsard, Thibault Pichon, Marin Prieur, Samuel Ronayette, Thierry Tourrette, François Visticot, Ludovic Genolet, Enrico Bozzo, Andras Peter Joo, Bendegúz Koncz, Rebeka Kiss, Viktor L. Toth, Henri Triou, Mickaël Lacroix
Items.Title: Preliminary design of the camera of the InfraRed Telescope of the THESEUS astronomy mission
Items.Abstract: The instrument InfraRed Telescope (IRT) of the THESEUS mission is composed of an Optical System and an Instrument Control System. The former includes the Telescope and the Camera subsystems. The Camera is mainly composed of a filter wheel, a focal plane and a calibration unit. It provides photometry in five bands in the 0.7 to 1.8 µm wavelength range as well as spectroscopy capability (0.8-1.6 µm) with a grating prism for the brightest sources. Coupled to a dedicated scientific on-board software, the camera images are used to identify and localise the transient sources with a 5 arcsec precision. A photo-Z imaging technique is also applied on-board to estimate the redshift with 10% precision. The paper presents the technical choices done to propose a camera design compliant with the instrument performance, optimising the system resources and the technology maturity. The camera structure was breadboarded to demonstrate the appropriate thermoelastic behaviour of the proposed solution.

Items.Authors: Kevin Phan, David Chaparro, J. Zachary Gazak
Items.Title: Preprocessing Strategies for Robust Satellite Detection Across Variable SNR Regimes
Items.Abstract: Reliable optical satellite detection depends heavily on preprocessing, particularly in low-SNR conditions where dim objects can be confused with stellar clutter or sensor artifacts. We present a systematic evaluation of contrast-enhancing and star-removal preprocessing techniques and measure their impact on machine-learning detection performance across a broad range of SNR regimes. Our pipeline compares methods such as local contrast normalization, adaptive histogram equalization, high-pass filtering, temporal stacking, and star-streak suppression. In particular, star-streak removal reduces confusion between elongated stellar PSFs and slow-moving satellites. Using real telescope imagery and controlled SNR simulations, we quantify changes in robustness, false positives, and F1 score. Results show that tailored preprocessing pipelines can significantly improve detector reliability and reduce annotation burden across diverse observing conditions.

Items.Authors: Maria Bergomi
Items.Title: Procurement complexities in custom astronomical optics and beyond
Items.Abstract: The acquisition of customized optical components represents one the most critical and time-consuming procurement while developing and managing complex astronomical instruments. In fact, it impacts all PM main areas: budget, timeline, performance and risk.   This work aims at making the full community – both on the instrument and company sides - aware of the difficulties encountered in such procurements, which have the peculiarity of presenting cutting-edge complexities to increase performance. It aims to present useful guidelines on the requirement definitions, including all terms of contract to reduce risk on the final result and useful lessons learned while experiencing procurement mainly in the context of ground-based instrumentation for large telescopes, with specific cases taken as example. The importance of the definition of clear requirements and all terms of the contract will be stressed, while considerations on possible strategies to reduce procurement risk will be discussed.

Items.Authors: Alessandro Morello, Desirée Della Monica Ferreira, Lars Buchhave, Irfan Kuvvetli, David Blanquez, Denis Tcherniak, Søren Møller, Gabriel Tello
Items.Title: Product and quality assurance strategies for space instrumentation development: from power electronics to structural and software qualification
Items.Abstract: This talk presents Product and Quality Assurance (PA/QA) activities at DTU Space for ESA missions LISA, ARIEL, and THESEUS. PA/QA ensures compliance with standards like ECSS and ISO 9001, reducing risks and guaranteeing mission success. For LISA PSM, the biggest challenge is the design of a custom DC/DC converter with related qualifications and tests. ARIEL activities verify CFRP bipods through material checks and structural tests. For THESEUS, assurance extends to software, emphasizing robust algorithms and independent verification. These examples show how PA/QA enables reliable, innovative space systems.

Items.Authors: Rainer Köhler, Robert Ligon, Narsireddy Anugu, Christopher Farrington, Douglas R. Gies, Karolina Kubiak, Cyprien Lanthermann, Gail Schaefer, Nic Scott, Nils Turner
Items.Title: Progress on integrating the mobile telescope into the CHARA array
Items.Abstract: The CHARA Array consists of 6 telescopes at fixed positions, connected by vacuum pipes to the central beam combiner.  The CHARA Michelson Array Pathfinder (CMAP) project includes two major components: 1) a mobile telescope that can be placed at a number of locations, and 2) a fiber optic relay system to transport light to the existing delay lines and beam combiners.  The mobile telescope is a 1m Ritchey-Chrétien system built by PlaneWave Instruments, equipped with a custom-built instrument bench with Adaptive Optics and fiber injection.  It is mounted in a custom enclosure on a trailer that can be moved around Mount Wilson Observatory.  In this contribution, we present the progress on the various subsystems needed to integrate the new telescope and beam transport method into the existing CHARA hardware and software environment.

Items.Authors: Weiwei Cui, Hao Wang, Yong Chen
Items.Title: Progress on the Spectroscopic Focusing Array-Imaging (SFA-I) Telescope onboard eXTP
Items.Abstract: Motivated by the exceptional on-orbit imaging performance and high sensitivity demonstrated by EP-FXT , the enhanced X-ray Timing and Polarimetry (eXTP) Science Team has concluded that its technical characteristics are ideally aligned with eXTP’s scientific objectives and are expected to significantly expand the mission’s scientific yield. Consequently, the project has resolved to incorporate an additional instrument whose configuration is equivalent to that of FXT, replacing one of the existing the Spectroscopy Focusing Array (SFA) units. The newly introduced payload, continuing to use the PNCCD supplied by MPE as its focal-plane detector, will be designated Design of the Spectroscopic Focusing Array-Imaging (SFA-I) in view of its imaging capabilities. SFA-I is designed to deliver a focal length of 5.25 m, an effective area ≥ 550 cm² at 1.5 keV (≥ 330 cm² at 6 keV), a field of view > 12′ × 12′, and an energy resolution ≤ 180 eV at 1.5 keV.

Items.Authors: Josh Walawender, Andrew Howard, Sam Halverson, Jeff Mader, Tyler Coda, Erik Petigura, Jack Lubin
Items.Title: Progress toward stable operations of the Keck Planet Finder
Items.Abstract: The Keck Planet Finder is a precision radial velocity, fiber fed, high resolution visible light spectrograph which was commissioned at the W. M. Keck Observatory in 2022. Since then, it has undergone 4 servicing missions. Some of the scientific goals of the instrument, however, require long term instrumental stability. Each servicing mission has affected observational programs which span the time across servicing missions. We present a summary of the operational challenges the work was designed to mitigate and the observatory's operational plan for achieving the decade long operational stability required by KPF's science goals.    Furthermore, achieving those long term science goals requires updates to the observatory's operational model. The cadenced observations which yield the best science are poor fit to a classically scheduled observatory. We will also present our scheme for KPF queue operations within a classically scheduled operational environment.

Items.Authors: Vincenzo Cianniello, Christian Eredia
Items.Title: Project management in support of an innovative engineering approach: the challenge of designing next-generation astronomical instrumentation
Items.Abstract: Designing next-generation astronomical infrastructures, such as large telescopes and advanced observational instruments, requires an integrated and systematic project management approach. These projects involve high technical complexity, interdependent mechanical, optical, and electronic systems, tight budgets, and schedules linked to multiple stakeholders, while demanding rigorous quality and safety standards.  Structured project management enables effective planning, monitoring, and control across the entire project lifecycle, from concept and preliminary design to construction, integration, testing, and commissioning. Strategic planning, cost and schedule control, knowledge management, and stakeholder communication are thus essential to transform innovative concepts into operational instruments, opening new window on the universe and positioning project management as a key enabler of engineering innovation in modern astronomy.

Items.Authors: Daniel R. Harbeck, Curtis McCully, Matt Daily, Prerana Kottapali
Items.Title: Propagating Random Telegraph Noise in Las Cumbres  Observatory’s CMOS data
Items.Abstract: At Las Cumbres Observatory we introduced CMOS-based imagers (QHY600 with Sony IMX455 sensors) as  the main cameras in our global network of ten 35-cm telescopes. The deployment of CMOS detectors in the small telescope network also serves as a pathfinder for a possible future. We report some of the first lessons learned from using CMOS cameras in a professional astronomy production environment. In particular, we focus on characterizing and treating random telegraph signal (RTS), an additional noise component in CMOS cameras. We have developed procedures to model RTS and then seed and propagate a simplified per-pixel noise model in our data processing pipeline BANZAI. We are exploring more advanced mitigation studies, such as using model such as using modeled multi-modal RTS distributions as a prior for maximum likelihood fitting when stacking images, which is capable of estimating a pixel’s true readout value with smaller samples than simple averaging.

Items.Authors: Lukas Stock, Andreas Schrimpf
Items.Title: PSF modeling for inexpensive off-the-shelf echelle spectrographs
Items.Abstract: Various spectroscopic target systems, such as close binary stars, require a very high cadence in the range of minutes to hours in order to determine their orbits using the radial velocity method. Due to limited observation time, this high cadence cannot be achieved by high-resolution spectrographs. However, for bright target systems (approx. Vmag <= 10), off-the-shelf echelle spectrographs on small telescopes (diameter <= 50 cm) can perform this task.  Due to their comparatively low price such instruments exhibit optical imperfections that limit the effective resolution of the instrument. Thus, ThAr calibration lines are distorted on the camera chip. I will present a way to increase the resolution through PSF modeling of these emission lines in the extraction software. This new extraction method is part of a new, open-source data reduction software written in Python 3, which I will also introduce.

Items.Authors: Martin M. Roth, Paško Roje, Stella Vješnica, Stefan Cikota, Alex J. Brown, Mike Kretlow, Marco Azzaro, Santiago Reinhart, Jesús Aceituno, Thomas Kupfer
Items.Title: qCMOS on sky: commissioning of the ORCA-TWIN project
Items.Abstract: Quanta image sensors have attracted attention for their unique capabilities for time domain astronomy and other applications requiring photon counting with high quantum efficiency and a large dynamic range, combined with very low noise and fast readout. The Hamamatsu ORCA-Quest 2 model C15550-22UP is an off-the-shelf camera delivering such capabilities. ORCA-TWIN is a fast track project of the emerging German Center for Astrophysics (DZA) that aspires to implement simultaneous observation at fast cadence from 1m class telescopes at two sites with a baseline of 1800 km, the Calar Alto and Teide observatories. We present the scientific rationale for LEOs, NEO and other solar system objects, as well as time domain astronomy, and first results form commissioning at Calar Alto.

Items.Authors: Valentin Emberger, Luisa Ostler, Johannes Müller-Seidlitz, Wolfgang Treberer-Treberspurg
Items.Title: Radiation effects and noise evolution in NewAthena WFI flight-production sensors
Items.Abstract: The Wide Field Imager (WFI), one of the two instruments aboard ESA’s upcoming large-class   X-ray observatory NewAthena, is optimized for imaging spectroscopy in the 0.2–15 keV energy range. Its focal plane comprises back-illuminated DEPFET sensors designed for high radiation tolerance. As part of the flight-production qualification, sensors were characterized to assess performance degradation induced by ionizing and non-ionizing radiation. The devices were irradiated with 62.4 MeV protons and 17.4 keV X-rays to total doses of   2.6 ∙ 10^9 10-MeV-protons/cm² and 1.5 krad, respectively. We present the resulting changes in readout noise, dark current, and threshold voltage, and compare them with the outcomes of a previous irradiation campaign on pre-flight devices. Implications for the required operating temperature and the expected end-of-life performance of the instrument are discussed.

Items.Authors: Fatima De Frondat Laadim, Julien Cailleux, Assia El Mouden, Nicola La Palombara, Jean-Laurent Dournaux, Giuseppe Leto, Cesare Molfese, Alessio Trois, Gianpiero Tagliaferri, Philippe Laporte, Hélène Sol, Andréas Zech, Alida Marchetti, Gianluca Giavitto, Richard White, Valentina Giordano, Fulvio Gianotti, Laura Proserpio, Giorgia Sironi, Gino Tosti, Ismam Abu, Claudio Arena, Carmelo Gargano, Pietro Giuseppe Bruno, William WANG, Salvatore Scuderi, Hiroyasu Tajima, Akira Okumura, James Anthony Hinton, Giovanni Pareschi, Christian Scaramozza, Ilaria Dal Ben, Gabriele Dal Ben, Filippo Dal Ben, Simone Piras, Luca Trevisan
Items.Title: RAMS analysis of small-sized telescopes (SST) for CTAO
Items.Abstract: The Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) will be the world’s largest and most sensitive ground-based gamma-ray telescope array, with sites in La Palma, Spain, and the Atacama Desert, Chile. Its goal is to study high-energy cosmic phenomena such as black holes, pulsars, and supernova remnants by detecting Cherenkov radiation produced when gamma rays interact with the atmosphere. The Small-sized Telescopes (SST) will focus on the highest energy range.    Given CTAO’s 30-year lifetime and the harsh desert environment, the project demands exceptional Reliability, Availability, Maintainability, and Safety (RAMS), aiming for 98.5% telescope availability. This paper presents the SST RAMS analysis, detailing the methodology, tools, and maintenance strategies developed collaboratively to ensure high performance, minimize downtime, and meet stringent operational and cost requirements.

Items.Authors: Yue Sun, Teng Xu, Jiangfang Jiang, Wei Wei, Chao Liu, Xuhao Wu, Changyu Zeng, Tao Wang, Guohua Zhou, Hemin Sun, Xiaofei Li, Junzhe Huang, Hang Zhang, Massinissa Hadjara, Yonghui Hou
Items.Title: Recent developments of 100m-baseline optical/infrared interferometer in China
Items.Abstract: China's 100-meter baseline optical/infrared interferometer is approaching completion. It consists of three 600mm-aperture telescopes, with primary scientific objectives including conducting high-precision astrometry and performing high-resolution imaging observations of bright stars. The deployment and testing of the three telescopes are expected to be completed in 2026, enabling the first fringe observations. This paper presents the recent developments of the facility, including updates on the telescopes, vacuum pipelines, delay lines, beam combiners, beam stabilization systems, and the pilot observations using siderostats.

Items.Authors: Yael Chich Prunenec, Pierre Bourget, Johan Kosmalski, Xavier Haubois, Nicolas Schuhler
Items.Title: Removing the optical derotators in the Auxiliary Telescopes of the VLTI for enhanced astrometry and system performance
Items.Abstract: This initiative for the Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) involves removing the optical derotators from its Auxiliary Telescopes (ATs), which are currently used to compensate for the field-of-view rotation. The derotators introduce issues such as polarization-dependent visibility loss, optical throughput degradation, and operational complexity due to tight alignment requirements. Eliminating the derotators aims to enable astrometry along the north-south baseline, reduce visibility loss, and simplify operations. The project covers opto-mechanical design adaptations, simulations, and testing, ensuring system compatibility.

Items.Authors: Niranjan A. Thatte, Michele Cappellari, Dimitra Rigopoulou, Miguel Pereira-Santaella, Ismael Garcia-Bernete
Items.Title: Removing wiggles in JWST IFS data by forward-modelling the PSF
Items.Abstract: JWST NIRSpec and MIRI-MRS IFS use image slicers to remap the 2D light distribution at a given wavelength into a set of narrow slitlets, which are then dispersed to form the raw detector images. For NIRSpec, the incoming light is divided into 30 slitlets, each dispersed over ~2000 spectral pixels on two detectors. The raw frames encode intensity as a function of wavelength and position along each slitlet. For point sources, however, under-sampling prevents an accurate reconstruction of a regularly sampled 3D cube using standard methods. Our solution is a forward-modelling approach in the detector plane. We model the response of the unresolved point source at every detector pixel and subtract it directly from the raw 2D frames. We fit a single scale factor per wavelength to match the observed PSF footprint, and thus recover the point-source spectrum. The spectrum will be used to scale and subtract the PSF from each exposure, allowing the pipeline to produce a wiggle-free 3D cube.

Items.Authors: Nicholas Herrald, Michael Copeland, Francis Bennet, Elisa Jager, Grace McGinness, Christopher Stokes-Griffin
Items.Title: Reporting on the "Moon to Mars" optical communication system mechanical design
Items.Abstract: A laser communications system was developed at Mt Stromlo Observatory in Canberra, to be compatible with the Optical to Orion laser communication system on the Artemis II mission. A Planewave RC700 telescope is used to receive signals from the space-craft with a transmit system mounted as an outrigger. A simple and robust optical design was employed for both the transmit and receive systems. System design and resulting performance is described. Both transmit and receive systems have shown a high degree of target and alignment stability over time, across integration cycles, exceeding system requirements under challenging conditions including fully sunlit daytime operations.

Items.Authors: Yoshihiko Saito, Yoshimi Rokugawa, Kenta Sakabe, Hideki Takami
Items.Title: Research and development of adaptive optics for satellite-to-ground laser communications at NICT in Japan
Items.Abstract: The demand for laser satellite communications is increasing due to the need for secure, high-capacity data transmission. Current systems remain in the demonstration stage, with atmospheric turbulence posing a major challenge to signal stability. Adaptive optics and fine pointing systems are essential to mitigate these effects and ensure reliable satellite-to-ground links. In Japan, the National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT) has deployed multiple optical ground stations equipped with such technologies. This paper presents NICT’s progress in adaptive optics development and outlines future directions for expanding laser satellite communication infrastructure.

Items.Authors: Wei Wei, Teng Xu, Fanghua Jiang, Yue Sun, Chao Liu, Xuhao Wu, Hemin Sun, Changyu Zeng, Tao Wang, Junzhe Huang, Yonghui Hou
Items.Title: Research and test observation progress of terminal subsystems of the Chinese Optical Infrared 100 m-Long Baseline Interferometer
Items.Abstract: The infrastructure construction of the Chinese Optical Infrared 100m-Long Baseline Interferometer has been completed. At present, three 600 mm aperture telescopes are being adjusted inside the dome, and the overall debugging of the interferometer is expected to be completed in 2026. During this period, with the aid of two 150 mm aperture fixed sky mirror systems, the subsystems in the interferometric terminal, including tilt correction system, time-domain fringe detection system and observation strategy generation system, were tested on a 57 m baseline, and the fringes of the target celestial bodies were successfully captured. This paper will introduce research and test observation progress of the terminal subsystem of the interferometer.

Items.Authors: Kimmy C. De Alba, Enrique De Alba, Thomas R. Swindle, Justin R. Fletcher
Items.Title: Rethinking Vision-First Cloud Detection in All-Sky Monitoring
Items.Abstract: Cloud detection from ground-based all-sky cameras is widely framed as a vision problem, with successive work pursuing more capable encoders. Whether this assumption holds at subregion granularity has not been directly tested. We evaluate three frozen encoder families alongside a baseline of curated statistical and metadata features and find all three converge to F1 scores between 0.81 and 0.82, while 15 observatory-derived features alone reach F1=0.87. Fusing frozen ResNet-50 embeddings with metadata does not significantly improve F1 but yields large gains in specificity (+0.08, p<0.001) and prevalence-aware normalized cost (-0.05, p<0.001), concentrating the visual channel's value in false-closure suppression. Our results suggest that metadata fusion and decision calibration yield larger returns than further backbone scaling under frozen extraction. More broadly, these findings caution against equating an image-based problem formulation with a vision-limited performance regime.

Items.Authors: Bruno Chazelas, Christophe Lovis, Nicolas Blind, Léonie Hoerner, Ludovic Genolet, Nathanael Restori, Ian Hughes, Michael Sordet, Robin Schnell, Samuel Rihs, Adrien Crausaz, David Ehrenreich, Emeline Bolmont, Christoph Mordasini, Martin Turbet, Maddalena Bugatti, Benoit Neichel, Thierry Fusco, Jean-François Sauvage, Isaac Bernardino Dinis, Angelie Alagao
Items.Title: RISTRETTO: assembly and testing of the seven-spaxel, high-resolution, diffraction-limited spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The RISTRETTO project aims at the direct detection of the reflected light of extra-solar planets to measure albedos and detect possible biosignatures, using the high-contrast / high-resolution method. We report on the assembly, lab-testing and on-sky testing of the seven-spaxel high-resolution single-mode spectrograph which was built ahead of the rest of the instrument.

Items.Authors: Cristian A. Rodriguez, Renate Kupke, Daren Dillion, Deno Stelter, Nicholas Mac Donald, Andy Skemer
Items.Title: SCALES spectrograph opto-mechanical design, manufacturing, and integration
Items.Abstract: Cryogenic infrared instruments inevitably face uncertainties in mechanical behavior during the transition from room temperature to operating temperature. Among the dominant effects are differential thermal contraction between dissimilar materials, micro-slip at mechanical interfaces, and distortion of parts arising from fabrication and material stresses. Cryogenic considerations aside, the size and performance requirements of the optics demanded extensive engineering to achieve manufacturability, structural rigidity, and stress-isolated mounting interfaces. This paper outlines the design strategies and manufacturing practices employed to minimise these effects and ensure reliable optical performance at operating temperature. These developments are for the spectrograph of the SCALES (Slicer Combined with an Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy) instrument, a 2–5 μm coronagraphic integral field spectrograph currently under construction for the W. M. Keck Observatory.

Items.Authors: Francisco Javier Veredas, Sebastian Albrecht, Robert Andritschke, Andreas Lederhuber, Marko Mecina, Roland Ottensamer, Kirpal Nandra, Miriam Ramos-Ceja
Items.Title: Science and telemetry data format for the NewAthena WFI instrument
Items.Abstract: We present the trade-offs on the data format for the WFI NewAthena instrument. The data network limitations and architecture of the WFI hardware are illustrated in terms of science data size and data rate. Previous missions and configuration options, along with the science data format, are also presented. Our investigations revealed that data compression is necessary to meet the current data budget requirements. Improvements to the science package size settings are also considered before each observation to enhance data throughput.

Items.Authors: Friederike Wolff
Items.Title: Science at scale: an analysis of organizational complexity in European planetary exploration missions
Items.Abstract: The days in which scientific breakthoughs could be performed by individual people working mostly autonomously have long passed. Especially in missions for space exploration, every new project is an undertaking of enormous scale in time, money, and people. The increasing complexity of technology gives rise to increasing specialization in technical domains, craftmanship, and managerial roles that raises new challenges on integrating all those domains of knowledge to produce a coherent result in a time-efficient manner. This paper describes the vastness of the systems that enable space mission to succeed, the organizational dynamics that arise from their sheer scale as well as how this impacts the day-to-day work of the individuals that contribute their seemingly tiny share to the overall endeavour.

Items.Authors: Edoardo Arrigoni, Sandro Mereghetti, Riccardo Campana, Alfonso Pisapia, Paolo Calabretto, Giulia Mattioli, Claudio Labanti, Enrico Virgili, Lorenzo Amati
Items.Title: Scientific performances of the XGIS instrument on-board THESEUS
Items.Abstract: The XGIS is a dual camera coded mask hard X-ray instrument on-board the THESEUS satellite (proposed ESA M7 mission) designed to detect high-energy transients inside its wide FoV and accurately localise them to allow rapid follow-up observations. We present the expected XGIS scientific performance obtained thanks to MC simulations of the instrument and to imaging simulation using the synthetic population of GRB derived from theoretical studies and the currently proposed self-supporting mask pattern design.

Items.Authors: Lique Lin, Lu Li, Yousong Yue
Items.Title: SDE-CraterNet: A Semantic Detail-Enhanced and Context-Aware Framework for Precise Martian Crater Segmentation
Items.Abstract: Precise boundary detection of Martian craters is vital for understanding the geological evolution and supporting autonomous navigation. However, existing methods face major limitations including confusion with crater-like terrain, semantic misalignment during feature fusion, and blurred boundary identification.  Thereforte, this study proposes a semantic-detail-enhanced and context-aware crater segmentation framework. To improve the accuracy of crater boundary segmentation, a Semantic Detail-Enhanced Upsampling Module is proposed, which incorporates crater-specific detailed information from high-resolution feature maps and corrects the semantic misalignment induced by upsampling. To enhance the capability of discriminating craters from morphologically similar landforms, Swin Transformer i semployed as the backbone network, leveraging its inherent attention mechanism that exhibits high compatibility with the circular structural characteristics of craters.

Items.Authors: Stephen Guzzo, Keith Cummings
Items.Title: Second generation DKIST data handling system
Items.Abstract: The National Science Foundation’s Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST) is a 4-meter solar observatory in operation at Haleakalā, Hawaii. The DKIST Data Handling System (DHS) is responsible for capturing science data from instrument cameras as well as metadata from telescope systems. After data acquisition is complete, the DHS converts data and metadata to FITS format and facilitates off-site transfer to a data center in Boulder, Colorado. After DKIST entered operations at the end of 2021, the observatory routinely produced data contingents of tens of terabytes (TB) per day that were sent to the data center. In order to accommodate the integration of future instruments as well as larger and faster camera sensors, we undertook an effort to redesign the DHS to improve performance and increase storage space. In this paper, we describe the motivation for this overhaul, give descriptions of both the hardware and software designs, give performance results, and discuss future improvements.

Items.Authors: Daniel S. Dahl, Nathan K. Long, Christopher H. Betters, Julia J. Bryant, Nick Cvetojevic, Michael Ireland, Stefan Kraus, Sergio Leon-Saval, Frantz Martinache, Marc-Antoine Martinod, Barnaby Norris, Jyotirmay Paul, Akira Rodziewicz-Ryan, Adam Taras, Jin Wei, Peter Tuthill
Items.Title: Seidr update: photonic ‘black magic’ for high-contrast interferometry using kernel-nulling and photonic lanterns
Items.Abstract: Seidr is a new interferometric beam combiner within the Asgard suite utilizing infrastructure common to the Bifrost instrument at the Very Large Telescope Interferometer. It combines hybrid mode-selective photonic lantern injection modules with a kernel-nulling photonic chip backend to enable deep H-band nulling for high-contrast studies of exoplanets, exomoons, and exo-zodiacal dust. This instrument update summarises Seidr’s current design maturity, recent simulations, and laboratory characterisation of both the lanterns and nulling chip, providing realistic expectations for on-sky performance. We also outline progress on a neural network–based wavefront correction scheme that uses higher-order lantern outputs to sense phase fluctuations and improve nulling stability.

Items.Authors: Domenico Barbato, Jacopo Farinato, Maria Bergomi, Elena Carolo, Simone Di Filippo, Valentina D'Orazi, Tania Sofia Gomes Machado, Fulvio Laudisio, Cecilia Lazzoni, Alessandro Lorenzetto, Luca Marafatto, Dino Mesa, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Davide Ricci, Daniele Vassallo
Items.Title: SHARK-NIR on the hunt: updates from early science runs and future horizons
Items.Abstract: SHARK-NIR is a near-infrared camera installed on the Large Binocular Telescope (LBT) in Arizona, performing high-contrast coronagraphic imaging, dual band imaging and low resolution spectroscopy in Y, J and H bands. Its main scientific goal is the search and characterization of exoplanets, exploiting the high performance of the LBT Adaptive Optics systems and synergic observations with SHARK-VIS (operating in V band) and LMIRCam (operating from K to M band) instruments on LBT.  Mounted on LBT in June 2022, SHARK-NIR first underwent a commissioning phase lasting until October 2023, aimed at testing its on-sky performance. An early-science phase followed, focusing on young exoplanets, protoplanetary disks, massive companions around accelerating stars and physical phenomena on minor bodies of the Solar System.  We present in this paper an updated description of SHARK-NIR, exploring its scientific output and the synergies with other instruments and exoplanetary detection methods.

Items.Authors: Bruce Lairson, James Tutt
Items.Title: Silicon carbide blocking filter grid geometries suitable for AXIS and newAthena
Items.Abstract: 4H-SiC single crystal X-ray grids have far higher strength and thermal conductance than the silicon used for XRISM grids. This results in X-ray blocking filters with higher strength and temperature uniformity, greatly mitigating issues such as launch durability and on-orbit signal decay. We present a design for a 76mm-aperture grid potentially suitable for the AXIS X-ray telescope, and a 128mm-aperture grid which could potentially be useful for the newAthena X-IFU entrance filter.

Items.Authors: Cyprien Lanthermann, Theo ten Brummelaar, Peter Tuthill, Narsireddy Anugu, Edgar R. Ligon, Adam Taras, Grace Piroscia, Gail Schaefer, Douglas R. Gies, Makoto Kishimoto
Items.Title: Silmaril: reducing the thermal background with a multi-stage narcissus mirror
Items.Abstract: Silmaril is a beam combiner at the CHARA Array designed for sensitivity, with the goal of reaching a limiting magnitude in the H- and K-band of 10. To reach this sensitivity in the K-band, we need to reduce the thermal background of the instrument, which is the dominant source of noise in K.  To do so, we use a Narcissus mirror, reflecting the thermal photons emitted by the cold camera (80 K) back to itself, except for the science beam going through specific holes placed in the mirror. In this presentation, we will describe the 2-stage design needed to overcome the physical limitations of the optical lab, and the design of the Narcissus mirrors to take into account the movement of the science beam pupils and the alignment process. We will then present the analysis of the resulting thermal-background reduction we obtain and compare it to the theoretical reduction of >90%.

Items.Authors: Klaus Subbotina Stephenson, Kate Jackson
Items.Title: Simulating multi-plane nlCWFSing with HCIPy
Items.Abstract: This work covers recent development of an open-source HCIPy based simulation for non-linear curvature wavefront sensing (nlCWFS). Proceeding a brief introduction on nlCWFSing, the authors dive into the methodology behind their simulation efforts and discuss research regarding the best conjugation distances for nlCWFS planes according to the quantified ability to correct for discrete Zernike modes, per the relationship between spatial frequency and propagation distance from the pupil plane.
